sections.h2: Who handles property tax in Green County, KY?
sections.html:
Two courthouse-area offices split the job in Green County. The Green County Sheriff collects the bill at 203 W Court Street, Greensburg, KY 42743, phone (270) 932-5641. The Property Valuation Administrator (PVA) assesses every parcel from 103 South 1st Street in Greensburg, phone (270) 932-7518.

The PVA values property and keeps the records. The sheriff takes payment. Call the PVA for address changes, exemption forms and questions about how a value was reached, and call ahead to either office to confirm its hours.

The Census counts 4,421 households in Green County, so a phone call to either office is the quickest way to confirm a payoff or a parcel record before you list.

sections.h2: What is Green County like for someone selling a house?
sections.html:
Green County is a rural county in south central Kentucky where Greensburg is the seat and the only incorporated city. Summersville is a census-designated place, and the 2020 census counted every resident as rural. The county was formed on December 20, 1792, from parts of Lincoln and Nelson counties, and it later gave up land to create Adair, Cumberland and Taylor counties.

The land covers about 286 square miles, and the Green River runs across it from east to west. The county government describes terrain that ranges from flat and gently rolling to steep and rocky, and it points to Green River Lake, American Legion Park on the river and Wyatt Jeffries Woods as local draws. Greensburg's 1804 brick courthouse, the oldest in the state according to Wikipedia, stands in the Downtown Greensburg Historic District, and the current courthouse dates from 1931. Cow Days brings crowds to town the third weekend of September.

Census QuickFacts gives the housing numbers sellers will meet:

  • Population estimate for July 2025: 11,644, up 4.8 percent from the 2020 base.
  • Owner-occupied housing rate: 77.6 percent. Persons per household: 2.54.
  • Median value of owner-occupied homes (2020 to 2024): $125,000.
  • Median owner costs: $955 a month with a mortgage and $361 without one.
  • Median gross rent: $610. Median household income: $46,798. Persons in poverty: 17.9 percent.

The county sits on the Central and Eastern time zone line, with LaRue and Taylor counties to the north on Eastern time, so check which clock an appointment uses.

sections.h2: What is the Green County property tax calendar?
sections.html:
The PVA posts a year-round calendar that starts with the January 1 assessment date and ends with the sheriff's settlement the following September. The key point for homeowners is that the sheriff holds the bill from mid September, the 2 percent discount ends November 1, and the first penalty arrives January 1. The same calendar lists a county clerk's sale of delinquent certificates from July 14 through August 28.

Green County real estate tax calendar (source: Green County PVA website)
StepDate or window
Tax roll open for inspection and PVA conferences13 days from the first Monday in May, six days a week
Board of assessment appeals5 days starting 25 to 35 days after inspection
Tax bills delivered to the sheriffBy September 15
Pay with discountBy November 1
Pay without discountNovember 2 to December 31
Pay with 5 percent penaltyJanuary 1 to January 31
10 percent penalty plus 10 percent sheriff's add-on feeAfter January 31
Unpaid bills move from sheriff to county clerkApril 15, after sheriff collects through close of business
Sheriff's settlementBy September 1

If bills are mailed late, the state can run a slower schedule that gives 30 days for each stage instead. The statute behind the main schedule is KRS 134.015.

sections.h2: How do I appeal a Green County assessment?
sections.html:
Meet with the Green County PVA first, then file with the county clerk. Under Kentucky's process an appeal to the local board of assessment appeals is closed to anyone who skipped the conference. The conference window is the 13-day inspection period that opens on the first Monday in May.

  • Ask the PVA to walk you through the assessment, then state the value you believe is right. The PVA's record of the conference lists the starting value, your claim and any changes agreed.
  • File the appeal at the clerk's office by the close of the workday after inspection ends.
  • Attend the board hearing and bring the proof: land and building details, insurance policies, build costs and sale listings of similar houses.
  • A decision to raise or lower the value must come with a written explanation from the board.

Anyone you pay to speak for you has to meet the state's list of qualified representatives and must carry your written authorization. Failing to file or to appear ends your right to continue to the Kentucky Claims Commission. If the bill was printed before the case ended and the final value is higher than you claimed, a supplemental bill follows for the difference.

sections.h2: Which Green County properties are exempt, and who gets the homestead break?
sections.html:
Kentucky's constitution exempts public property used for public purposes, burial grounds, church property, charities, schools not run for gain, public libraries, household goods and crops in the producer's hands, and the Green County PVA site reproduces that list. Homeowners get a separate break: age 65 or older, or totally disabled, with the home as a permanent residence.

The amount is $49,100 for the 2025 and 2026 assessment years. At Green County's Census median of $125,000, a qualifying owner would be taxed on $75,900. File the application with the PVA, with proof of age such as a birth certificate, driver's license or passport. Owners applying on disability must have received disability payments for the full assessment period and must reapply yearly, with exceptions for service-connected veterans and people found totally and permanently disabled by Social Security or Kentucky Retirement Systems.

If you move out, give the PVA your new mailing address so assessment notices and tax bills reach you.

sections.h2: What happens if I sell a Green County house with taxes unpaid?
sections.html:
The unpaid tax stays attached to the parcel, so the buyer inherits it unless it is paid at or before closing. Kentucky makes the tax the owner's personal debt as of the assessment date, and a lien from a delinquent bill continues until payment or the 11-year limit in KRS 134.420, regardless of who holds title.

Timing drives the cost. A bill paid to the sheriff before April 15 carries only the penalties already earned. After that date the County Clerk adds interest at 1 percent a month, plus the clerk's 10 percent commission, a county attorney commission and a lien fee. The Department of Revenue's worked example turns a $1,000 face bill into $1,387.79 if paid within five business days of the transfer and $1,611.30 after the county attorney's first notice.

The county attorney sends notices within 30 days and again within 60 days, and the tax sale falls 90 to 135 days after the transfer. Ask the sheriff and the clerk for written payoffs before you list, and have your closing agent pay both from the sale proceeds.

faqs.q: When is the Green County property tax discount deadline?
faqs.a: November 1. The PVA's calendar lists payment with the 2 percent discount by November 1, face amount from November 2 through December 31, and a 5 percent penalty during January.

faqs.q: Where do I pay property tax in Green County?
faqs.a: To the Green County Sheriff at 203 W Court Street in Greensburg, phone (270) 932-5641. The PVA at (270) 932-7518 values property and handles exemptions but does not take payments.

faqs.q: What is added after January 31 in Green County?
faqs.a: A 10 percent penalty plus a 10 percent sheriff's add-on fee, according to the PVA's calendar. From April 15 the bill sits with the County Clerk, where monthly interest and commissions are added.

faqs.q: How much is the homestead exemption in Green County?
faqs.a: It is $49,100 off assessed value for 2025 and 2026, for owners 65 or older or totally disabled. A house assessed at the county median of $125,000 would be taxed on $75,900.

faqs.q: When does Green County hold its tax sale of delinquent bills?
faqs.a: Between July 14 and August 28 under the normal calendar. State law puts the sale 90 to 135 days after unpaid bills move from the sheriff to the County Clerk on April 15.
